# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👌 ✌ ✌ 👌 👍]

I need to think about this carefully. I'm the Deaf monkey - I can see the bomb but not hear speech. Mute just gestured to me, since I can see gestures.

Let me note what I see on the bomb:
- DISPLAY shows [0]
- LIGHT is yellow
- BUTTON is large, labeled "PUSH TO DEFUSE"
- WIRES: 1:blue, 2:yellow, 3:red

Mute gestured to me: [👍 👌 ✌ ✌ 👌 👍]

I don't yet know what this means - no meaning has been established yet. Since it's turn 1, Mute is likely trying to establish a code, or asking me something about the bomb using a prearranged scheme from the manual. But nothing has been defined yet between us, so I can't decode this without more context.

Since Blind cannot see gestures or read, I can only communicate with Blind through speech. Mute can gesture to me and speak to Blind. I should report what I see to Mute (via speech, since Mute cannot hear speech either - wait, Mute cannot speak or touch, but can Mute hear? Let me check - the table doesn't say Mute cannot hear. Only Deaf cannot hear. So Mute CAN hear my speech.

So I should speak my findings to Mute (who can hear me), and gesture is only useful for Mute to send to me, not vice versa in a way that matters - actually I could gesture back to Mute too if needed, but speech is more direct since Mute hears.

Let me report the full bomb state to Mute via speech, since Mute needs this info to cross-reference with the manual.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Display shows zero. Light is yellow. Button is large labeled push to defeat. Wire 1 is blue, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is red. I saw your gesture but do not yet know what it means, please explain via speech since I cannot hear you, so instead describe simply or repeat gestures with clearer meaning.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝]

I need to fix my gesture call - it needs a `symbols` argument, not text.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Bomb state: display shows zero, light is yellow, large button labeled push to defuse, three wires - wire 1 blue, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 red. Waiting on manual instructions from mute relayed through me.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute keeps gesturing simple things: first "thumbs up, ok, victory, victory, ok, thumbs up", then three "point up" gestures, now a single thumbs up. This looks like Mute is trying to build a simple yes/no or acknowledgment protocol with me since we have no shared language yet.

The ☝☝☝ (point up x3) might have meant "wire 3" or "look at wire 3" or "third item". Now 👍 alone might mean "yes/correct" - possibly confirming something, or asking if I understand.

Since I can't respond meaningfully without more clarity, and Mute cannot hear gestures back interpretation but CAN hear speech - I should keep relaying bomb facts to Blind (who needs to act) and try to establish a simple protocol with Mute using speech, since Mute can hear me even though Mute cannot speak back.

Let me propose a protocol to Mute: use gestures like thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no, and I'll ask yes/no questions about the bomb via speech that Mute can hear, then Mute gestures back yes/no.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I will ask yes or no questions about the manual. Please gesture thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no. Does the manual instructions depend on the wire colors?")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤝"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute gestured 👍 again - this could be confirming "yes" to my proposed protocol (thumbs up = yes), or it's a coincidental repeat. Given the timing, this is likely Mute agreeing to my yes/no protocol proposal, OR answering my question "does it depend on wire colors" with yes.

Let me continue building the protocol carefully, asking one clear question at a time so I can distinguish protocol-confirmation from actual answers.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Good, thumbs up means yes. I will now ask about the display and light too. Does the manual instruction depend on the display number, which currently shows zero?")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

Mute gestured 👎 - "no". So the manual instruction does NOT depend on the display number. Combined with the earlier 👍 to "does it depend on wire colors" - it seems wire colors matter.

Let me continue narrowing down what matters: light color, button, etc.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Understood, display number does not matter. Does the instruction depend on the light color, which is currently yellow?")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Light color matters too (👍 = yes). So far: wire colors matter (yes), display doesn't matter (no), light color matters (yes).

Now I need to figure out exactly what to do - which wire to cut, or whether to push the button. Let me ask about the button and then try to narrow down the specific wire action.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Light color matters too. Does the instruction depend on the button, meaning should blind push the button as part of the solution?")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

Button doesn't matter (no push). So it's about cutting a wire, and it depends on wire colors and light color. Since light is yellow, and wire 2 is also yellow - this could be significant (a common bomb trope: cut the wire matching the light color, or avoid it).

Let me ask specifically about which wire to cut.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Understood, no button push. It seems the wire to cut depends on both wire colors and the light color. The light is yellow and wire 2 is also yellow. Should blind cut the wire that matches the light color, meaning wire 2?")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

Not wire 2 (the one matching light color). So the rule might be the opposite - avoid the matching color, or it's a different logic entirely (like "if light is yellow, cut the wire that ISN'T yellow" or specific wire number regardless of color, or maybe it depends on order/count of colors).

Let me ask more targeted questions - try wire 1, wire 3, or ask if it's about avoiding the matching color.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Not wire 2. Is the rule instead to avoid the wire matching the light color, meaning cut a different wire, either wire 1 blue or wire 3 red?")
```
